title: Waves of moving particles
hook: Change kinetic energy and predict de Broglie wavelength.
misconception: de Broglie wavelength doubles when kinetic energy doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply λ = h/√(2mK) to compare de Broglie wavelength when kinetic energy changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic particle of fixed mass with positive kinetic energy, λ = h/√(2mK). When kinetic energy doubles, de Broglie wavelength becomes 1/√2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model λ = h/√(2mK); scaling exponent -0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic particle of fixed mass with positive kinetic energy, with a nonzero initial result. If kinetic energy triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on de Broglie wavelength?
recall.why: Apply λ = h/√(2mK) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/√3.
